name: Nine-Card Don
description: Nine-Card Don (also known as Big Don or Welsh Don) is a traditional British pub game for four players in fixed partnerships. It is a descendant of the 17th-century game All Fours. Unlike the Irish version, only nine cards are dealt to each player, leaving a significant portion of the deck unseen, which adds a layer of uncertainty and boneyard-tracking to the strategy.

content.text: Nine-Card Don (also known as Big Don or Welsh Don) is a traditional British pub game for four players in fixed partnerships. It is a descendant of the 17th-century game All Fours. Unlike the Irish version, only nine cards are dealt to each player, leaving a significant portion of the deck unseen, which adds a layer of uncertainty and boneyard-tracking to the strategy.
Don evolved from Dom Pedro in the 19th century. While Ireland developed the 13ndcard version, British players in Cheshire, Lancashire, and South Wales standardized the 9ndcard version.
Each player receives 9 cards (dealt in batches of 3). The remaining 16 cards are set aside and not used in the hand.
